Reference / web/app

web/app#

Binds a route table to a listener: HTTP/1.1 in cleartext, or HTTPS with HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 offered by ALPN (#80).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

await WebApplication(routes).listen(address: "127.0.0.1", port: 8000);
await WebApplication(routes).listen(address: "0.0.0.0", port: 8443, tls: identity);

Description#

Binds a route table to a listener: HTTP/1.1 in cleartext, or HTTPS with HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 offered by ALPN (#80).

listen() serves until SIGTERM or SIGINT: then the server stops accepting, gives the requests in flight 10 seconds to finish, closes, and listen() drains its logger (StderrLogs waits at most two seconds) and returns. A second signal ends the process at once. The address is an IP literal; no name resolution happens here. server() binds and returns the std HttpServer without serving, for callers that own the lifetime themselves: port 0 picks a free port, local_endpoint() reports it, and server.drain(limit:) drains it.

Public API#

object WebApplication#

object WebApplication does Handling

A route table served on an address and port. Pass logger: to log every completed request, including 404s and fallbacks; the default logs nothing. Exceptions keep their HTTP status at info; other errors log 500 at error with their cause and propagate. The request never carries the logger.

WebApplication.WebApplication#

WebApplication(routes is WebRoutes, logger is Logger = Logger(name: "web", destination: DiscardingLogs()))

Serves routes with the default policy. logger logs completed requests at info, or unhandled errors at error with their cause; omitted, it is silent. Lines are "GET /notes?limit=5 200 0.412 ms", with an address field.

WebApplication.WebApplication#

WebApplication(routes is WebRoutes, policy is ServerPolicy, clock is Timing, logger is Logger = Logger(name: "web", destination: DiscardingLogs()))

Serves routes with policy, timing requests on clock. logger has the same line, levels and address field as above; omitted, it logs nothing.

WebApplication.server#

async server(address is string, port is int) is HttpServer

The server knows its own URL, so a WebSocket route can check the Origin of an upgrade against it.

HTTPS: the identity's certificate and key, HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 by ALPN.

WebApplication.server#

async server(address is string, port is int, tls is TlsIdentity) is HttpServer

The HTTPS server, bound and not serving; its own URL is https.

WebApplication.handling#

async handling(request is Request, context is HttpRequestContext) is HandlingResult

Handles a request through the server's pipeline, including its log. WebTestClient(application) exercises it without a listener.
